nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $t$ be lists over a type with a lawful boolean equality, with $p$ nonempty. Let the first-infix split of $t$ by $p$ be the pair $(u, v)$ with $t = u \, p \, v$ (concatenation) and $u$ as short as possible, or nothing if $p$ does not occur in $t$. Then the value returned by KMP search for $p$ in $t$ is the length of $u$ if the split exists, and no offset otherwise.
nodes.title: KMP search agrees with the first-infix split

nodes.summary: For lists $p$ (the pattern) and $t$ (the text) over a type with a lawful boolean equality, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns no offset if and only if $p$ is not a contiguous sublist of $t$, that is, there are no lists $u$, $v$ with $t = u \, p \, v$ (concatenation).
nodes.title: KMP finds no match exactly when the pattern does not occur

nodes.summary: For lists $p$ and $t$ over a type with a lawful boolean equality, write $|t|$ for the length of $t$. KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns no offset if and only if there is no natural number $i$ at which $p$ matches $t$, where $p$ matches $t$ at $i$ when $i \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $t$ by dropping its first $i$ elements.
nodes.title: KMP finds no match exactly when no offset matches

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $t$ be lists over a type with a lawful boolean equality, and write $|t|$ for the length of $t$. For every natural number $i$, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns the offset $i$ if and only if $p$ matches $t$ at $i$ and at no $j < i$, where $p$ matches $t$ at $i$ when $i \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $t$ by dropping its first $i$ elements.
nodes.title: KMP returns the first match

nodes.summary: For every text $t$, KMP search for the empty pattern in $t$ returns offset $0$ at cost $0$, that is, without any symbol comparisons.
nodes.title: KMP search on the empty pattern

nodes.summary: For any pattern $p$ and text $t$, lists over a type with a boolean equality, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ makes at most $2|p| + 2|t|$ symbol comparisons in total, those made while building the prefix table included, where $|p|$ and $|t|$ are the lengths of $p$ and $t$.
nodes.title: KMP search makes linearly many comparisons

nodes.summary: For lists $p$ (the pattern) and $t$ (the text) over a type with a boolean equality, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns either a zero-based offset or no offset, together with a cost: the number of symbol comparisons it makes. If $p$ is empty, it returns the offset $0$ at cost $0$. Otherwise it first builds the prefix table of $p$, a list of entries each pairing a symbol with a failure value. The transition of a table…
nodes.title: Knuth–Morris–Pratt search

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a pattern of length $n$ over a type with a lawful boolean equality, and write $p_{\lt k}$ for its prefix of length $k$. Each entry of the KMP prefix table of $p$ pairs a symbol of $p$ with a failure value. For every $q < n$, the failure value $f$ of entry $q$ (counting from $0$) is the length of the longest proper prefix of $p_{\lt q+1}$ that is also a suffix of $p_{\lt q+1}$: $f \le q$, $p_{\lt f}$ is a…
nodes.title: The KMP failure function

nodes.summary: For every pattern $p$, the KMP prefix table of $p$ has exactly as many entries as $p$ has symbols, one for each symbol of $p$.
nodes.title: Size of the KMP prefix table

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a pattern of length $n$ over a type with a lawful boolean equality, and write $p_{\lt k}$ for its prefix of length $k$. Let $c$ be a list, $x$ a symbol, and $cx$ the list $c$ followed by $x$. Suppose the state $s \le n$ is the length of the longest prefix of $p$ that is a suffix of $c$: $p_{\lt s}$ is a suffix of $c$, and every $k \le n$ such that $p_{\lt k}$ is a suffix of $c$ satisfies $k \le s$. nodes.title: Correctness of the KMP transition

nodes.summary: Each entry of the Knuth–Morris–Pratt prefix table is a pair consisting of a symbol and a failure length. For every type with a Boolean equality test and every list $p$ over it, the list of first components of the entries of the prefix table built from $p$, read in order, equals $p$.
nodes.title: The KMP prefix table stores the pattern

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
